_comment: FACTORtv — THE BOOTH KNOWS WHOSE CAREER THIS IS.
The commentary is most of the gameplay, and until now it knew the race, the
circuit, the cars and the real drivers — and nothing whatsoever about the
career being played. A man in his third season of Formula 3, who won karting
two years ago and has a Formula 2 seat riding on this afternoon, was called
'the driver in fourth'.
EVERY LINE HERE IS TRUE BY CONSTRUCTION. The facts come from
`Career.resume()` and `Career.evaluate()` — seasons this overlay recorded,
races it watched, championships it scored. Nothing is invented and nothing
needs a knowledge base, which is why these work identically in a karting
field and in Formula One. That is the whole reason the ladder can be
commentated at all: a GT4 mod's AI has no record anywhere, but the PLAYER's
record is something we watched happen.
SLOTS:
{drv} the name he races under     {series} the division he is in now
{below} the division beneath it   {need} the position the next seat needs
{seasons} seasons completed       {races} races started
{wins} race wins in this career   {titles} championships won
{n} a count, in words             {left} rounds left in the season
REGISTER IS A TONE, NOT A KNOWLEDGE BASE. `reg_*` pools say what KIND of
racing this is — a club meeting, a junior category with everybody watching,
a professional championship. Karting commentary is not Formula One
commentary, but the difference is how it SOUNDS, and tone is cheap while
invented history is not.

ladder_first_race.t: First time out in {series} for {drv}. New car, new field, and everything he knew last season is now a starting point rather than an answer.
This is {drv}'s first race in {series}, and there is no gentle way into a category like this one.
A debut for {drv} at this level. The first few rounds of a step up are about learning what the car will not let you do.

ladder_reigning.t: {drv} arrives here as the reigning {below} champion — and a title in the category below buys you precisely nothing on a Sunday.
The {below} champion, stepping up. Everybody in this paddock has watched somebody do that and disappear, and watched somebody else do it and never look back.
{drv}, who won {below} last season, is out there learning what the difference between these two categories actually is.

ladder_climb.t: {drv} has come up through every rung of this thing — {seasons} seasons of it, and none of them handed to him.
{races} races into a career that started at the bottom of the ladder. That is the unglamorous version of how a driver gets here.
It has taken {drv} {seasons} seasons to get to this grid, which is about normal, and it is the part nobody puts in a highlight reel.

ladder_record.t: {wins} race wins for {drv} across this career now, in four different kinds of car.
That is {titles} championships to his name — and Chuck, they were not won in the same machinery.
{wins} wins and {titles} titles. A record like that gets a driver looked at differently in the room before a race, never mind on the circuit.

ladder_arc.t: {drv} has already won a championship in another discipline entirely, which is rarer than it sounds and harder than it looks.
A man who has been champion elsewhere. Different cars, different tyres, different way of racing — and he came here and started again.
Whatever happens this afternoon, {drv} has a title in another category on his record. Very few drivers ever manage two.

ladder_promotion.t: There is a seat above this championship, and {need} in the final standings is what it costs. {drv} knows exactly what the number is.
Everything this season is worth is decided by where he finishes it. {need} gets him out of {series}; anything less and he is here again next year.
That is what makes these afternoons matter — not the trophy, the seat it unlocks.

ladder_last_chance.t: Last round of the season, and {drv} is racing for a promotion rather than a trophy. {need} or another year in {series}.
Everything he has done this season comes down to the next hour. A seat above this category is on the line, and it is decided today.
This is the afternoon a career turns on, and there is no consolation version of it. He either takes the seat or he does not.

ladder_title_run.t: {left} rounds left, and {drv} is fighting for a championship that decides where he races next season.
The title here is not the end of it. A championship in this category is a ticket out of it, and everybody on this grid is racing for the same door.
{left} rounds left and everything still to play for. This is where seasons are actually decided — not in the last race, in the two before it.
The maths has started mattering. {left} rounds, and every point {drv} leaves out there is one he has to find again somewhere else.

reg_grassroots.t: No television money in this paddock. Everybody here is paying for their own tyres, and half of them drove the transporter themselves.
This is where it starts for almost everybody. Small grids, small budgets, and results that follow a driver around for the rest of his career.
A club meeting on a Sunday afternoon, and I promise you the racing is no less serious for it.
Nobody out there is being paid to do this. That is worth remembering when you watch how hard they are going at it.
Somebody in this paddock is going to be a world champion one day, and right now he is helping his dad load a trailer.
Entry fees, a van, and a weekend. That is the whole budget for most of these cars.

reg_junior.t: A junior category, which means every driver out there is being watched by somebody with a seat to fill further up.
Careers are made and quietly ended in categories like this one, usually before anybody outside the paddock has heard the names.
Equal machinery, near enough, which means there is nowhere for a driver to hide out there.
The gap between the best of these and the rest is smaller than at any other level of the sport, and it decides everything.
Every driver here is being measured against his team mate, and everybody in the sport knows that is the only comparison that means anything.
This is the level where a career either starts or quietly stops. Nobody says so out loud, and everybody out there knows it.

reg_professional.t: Professional racing, professional consequences. Every one of these drivers is somebody's employee, and results are how the contract gets renewed.
This is the level everybody down there is climbing towards, and it is unforgiving in a way the categories below it are not.
Big teams, big operations, and a driver who is one bad season from being replaced by somebody cheaper and younger.
There is money in this paddock now, and money brings expectation. Every one of these drivers is being judged against a contract.
The racing at this level is the closest thing the sport has to a fair fight, and it is completely merciless.
Nobody arrives here by accident. Every driver on this grid has spent a decade getting to it.

ladder_home.t: And this is a home race for {drv}. Whatever else happens this afternoon, he will hear the difference from the grandstands.
{drv} is racing at home today. Every driver says it makes no difference, and every driver who has done it knows that is not quite true.
A home crowd for {drv} — and a home crowd is the only pressure in this sport that nobody has ever worked out how to prepare for.
This one is in his own country, and there will be people in that grandstand who watched him race karts.
A home race for {drv}. The one weekend a year a driver hears his own name from the grandstand before he has done anything.

ladder_home_win.t: A home win. There is nothing else in this sport quite like it, and most drivers never get one.
He has won his home race. Ask any driver on that grid which victory they would take, and this is the one they would name.
Winning at home. Drivers spend entire careers trying to arrange that afternoon and most of them never manage it.

ladder_nation.t: {drv}, the {nat}, out there in the middle of it.
There are not many {nat} drivers at this level, which makes {drv} worth watching on that alone.
{drv} carries a {adj} licence, and he has come a very long way from home to be on this grid.
{drv} is a long way from home this weekend, which is the ordinary condition of a racing driver and never stops being strange.
The {nat} in the field — and there have not been many of those at this level.

status_rookie.t: {drv} is a rookie in the truest sense of it — nobody in this paddock has any idea yet what he is going to turn into.
{drv}. And Chuck, nobody in this paddock has any idea yet what he is going to turn into.
A rookie out there, and rookies are the most interesting drivers on any grid — because nobody has decided what they are yet.
This is a driver at the very start of it. Everything he does this season is the first time he has ever done it.
Nobody knows what {drv} is yet, and that includes {drv}. That is what a first season actually is.
A rookie gives himself away in the small things - a little too much steering on the way in, a little too much throttle on the way out. It goes away.
The interesting thing about a rookie is that everything he learns in his first season, he keeps.
{drv} has nothing behind him at all. No record, no reputation, nobody expecting anything — which is a freedom he will never have again.
First season. Everybody on this grid was here once, and most of them will tell you it was the most frightened they have ever been in a car.

status_riser.t: {drv} was a rookie not so long ago. He has climbed out of {below} since then, and he is not being called a rookie for much longer.
This one is on his way up. A division a year, and the people who fill seats above this level have started asking about him.
{drv} has already earned his way out of one championship. That is the hard part, and most drivers never manage it once.
{drv} is going the right way. Not the fastest man out there yet, but a driver who is a different proposition every time we see him.
A season or two ago nobody in this paddock could have picked {drv} out of a line-up. That has stopped being true.
This is the awkward stage of a career — good enough to be noticed, not yet good enough to be safe. Most drivers do not survive it.

status_contender.t: The rookie is gone. {drv} is starting to look like a genuine contender at this level, and that is a different conversation entirely.
{drv} arrived here as a kid nobody had heard of and he is now racing people who have been doing this for a living for years — on level terms.
A contender. Not a prospect, not a name for the future — a man who can win this championship, in this car, this season.
{drv} is being talked about now by the sort of people whose opinion decides where a driver races next year.
He has arrived at the level where nobody cares what you did in the category below. And he is holding his own.
There is a difference between a driver who is quick and a driver who is a problem, Chuck, and {drv} has crossed it.

status_champion.t: {drv}, a champion in this sport now, and nobody can ever take that sentence away from him.
There is a championship on {drv}'s record, and it changes how every driver on this grid races him.
The champion. He came into this sport with nothing at all and he has a title on the board.
A champion out there. He drives the same as he did a year ago; everybody else races him differently.
{drv} has the one thing in this sport that cannot be bought, borrowed or explained away — a championship with his name on it.

status_multi.t: {titles} championships for {drv} now. One can be a season that went right; two is a driver.
A multiple champion out there. That is a very short list in any category, and he is on it.
{drv} has won this sport's championships in more than one machine, which is the only test that has ever meant anything.
Two titles and counting. The paddock has stopped asking whether {drv} can win one and started asking who is going to stop him.
{titles} championships in different machinery. That is the only comparison this sport has ever accepted as meaningful.

status_legend.t: {titles} championships. At some point you stop calling a man a great driver and start calling him a part of the sport's history — {drv} is past that point.
A legend of this sport, out there in the middle of a race like anybody else. There is nothing left for him to prove to anyone.
{drv}. Karting to this, {titles} titles, and a career people will still be arguing about long after he stops.
There are drivers on this grid who were watching {drv} on television when they decided to do this for a living.
A career like this one comes along about once a decade, and we are watching the end of it happen in real time.

status_arrival.t: From rookie to champion. {drv} has had a meteoric rise in this sport, and I cannot wait to see what he does next.
He arrived with nothing and no record and nobody expecting anything, and he leaves this season as a champion. That is the whole sport in one career.
From a kart to this. {drv} is a champion, and every one of us watched him earn it a division at a time.
He was a rookie nobody had heard of, and he is a champion. That is the whole sport, in one career, in front of us.

status_arrival_more.t: {titles} championships now for {drv}, and this one was won in front of people who remember him as a rookie.
Another title. He is not a story any more — he is a record, and the record is still being written.
Another one. {drv} is no longer a driver having a good run — he is a record, and it is still being added to.

ladder_rivalry.t: {b} and {drv} have finished within a place of each other in most of the last few rounds, and there are {pts} points between them. This is the fight of the season.
These two keep arriving at the same corner at the same moment. {pts} points apart, and neither of them is going away.
Chuck, this has stopped being a coincidence — {drv} and {b} have raced each other in every round for weeks.
Every time one of them finds something, the other one finds it a fortnight later. {pts} points between them and no sign of that changing.
This has become the story of the season, and neither garage is pretending otherwise. Two drivers, {pts} points, and a great many rounds still to run.
Watch where {b} places his car when {drv} is behind him. That is not how you defend against somebody you are comfortable about.

ladder_needle.t: And {b} had a few things to say about {drv} in the press this week, none of which will have gone unnoticed in that garage.
There is a bit of needle here now. {b} was asked about {drv} at the last event and gave an answer that was not exactly warm.
Whatever was said in the press conference, these two are racing each other harder than they are racing anybody else.
{b} has been quoted this week on the subject of {drv}, and Miles, drivers do not talk about people they are not worried about.
These two are not speaking, and the paddock has noticed. It has not made either of them slower.
There has been a bit said in the press this week, and both of them are about to have to answer for it out on the circuit.
{b} was asked about {drv} again this week. He has stopped pretending he has not noticed him.

prog_stake.t: {drv} is racing this season with {prog} behind him, and that is a different kind of pressure to the one on everybody else out here.
There is a Formula One programme watching this car. {prog} do not put their name on a driver and then look away.
Every lap of this season is being watched by people who can end it, and {drv} knows exactly who they are.
{prog} are behind him this year. A seat at {f1team} is what that means if it works, and nothing at all if it does not.
He is not only racing a championship here — he is auditioning, and everybody in this paddock knows it.

prog_last_chance.t: This is the afternoon it is decided. Win this championship and a Formula One seat is his; finish second and it is another year of asking.
{prog} have made the terms plain, and they come down to today: the title, or nothing.
Everything {drv} has done this season comes to this race, and there is a seat at {f1team} on the other side of it.
A championship and a Formula One drive, in one afternoon. There is no version of this where second place is enough.

prog_debut.t: This is his first Grand Prix. {drv} takes the {f1team} seat, alongside {lead}, and a year of waiting ends right here.
A Formula 2 champion, a year in development, and now the other side of {lead}'s garage. That is the whole climb, in one sentence.
{drv} arrives at {f1team} the long way round — a title, a year out of the car, and a seat nobody handed him.
He spent a season out of a racing car for this. Now he is in one, and it is a {f1team}, and the man he is measured against is {lead}.

prog_measured.t: There is nowhere to hide in this seat. {lead} is in the same car, and that is the only comparison anybody at {f1team} will make.
{drv} was put in this car by people who wanted to find something out. This season is the answer, one way or the other.
The hardest part of arriving here is not the speed, it is the other side of the garage. {lead} has been doing this for years.

prog_callup_debut.t: This is {drv}'s first time racing this car. He was in Formula 3 a fortnight ago, {f2team} made a change, and here he is.
A mid-season call-up for {drv}, and no test to prepare for it. The seat came free, {prog} put their own driver in it, and this is the afternoon that starts.
Worth saying what we are watching: {drv} has been handed a seat at {f2team} with the season already running. Nothing about that is normal and everybody in that garage knows it.
He has not raced this car before today. {prog} moved him up when the seat opened, and the first laps he does in anger are the ones we are about to watch.

prog_callup_stake.t: {drv} is in this car because {f2team} changed their line-up mid-season. What he does with the rest of it decides whether he keeps it.
Remember he arrived here with the season part-run and nothing on the board. Every point he has, he has scored since.
A replacement driver is asked a narrow question, and {drv} is being asked it in public, one weekend at a time.
{prog} did not promote him for winning anything. They promoted him because a seat came free and they had somebody they wanted to look at.

prog_bar_chase.t: {drv} is {pos} in this championship and {gap} points off {rival}, who holds the {bar} place his programme has told him to reach.
The number that matters to {drv} is not the leader's. It is {rival}'s - {gap} points up the road in {bar}, with {left} rounds to run.
{gap} points, {left} rounds, and one position. That is {drv}'s season, and it is a strange way to have to race.
He needs to finish {bar} in the standings for the seat above to open. He is {pos}. Everything else out here is detail.

prog_bar_hold.t: {drv} is {pos} in the standings, which is exactly where he needs to be - and {rival} is {gap} points behind him with {left} rounds left.
He is inside the mark his programme set, by {gap} points. From here it stops being a chase and starts being something he can lose.
{drv} came into this car with nothing and he is {pos}. What he is defending now is a Formula One seat, not a trophy.
{gap} points over {rival}, {left} rounds to go. Drivers will tell you defending a position is the hardest way to end a season.

prog_callup_last.t: Last round, and {drv} is {pos} with the {bar} place the whole thing depends on. {gap} points between him and {rival}.
This is it. Finish {bar} today and the Formula One seat opens; finish behind {rival} and it does not. {gap} points is the margin.
Everything {drv} has done since he was handed this car comes down to the next hour or so, and to one position in a table.
